discoveryNotes:
I used 10 standard WebSearch calls and no extended search or WebFetch. The search tool returns summaries: items marked (paraphrase) are the tool's summary, and quoted fragments are verbatim as returned.

AUTHORITY-LIST GAPS:
(1) No result returned the Ministry of Health of Ukraine's list of subordinate higher medical institutions (moh.gov.ua). As a result, Ministry of Health subordination is unconfirmed for every candidate here, including the National University of Pharmacy.
(2) The universities.studyinukraine.gov.ua directory (MES / Ukrainian State Centre for International Education) could not be filtered by specialty code (222/221/226/223) through search. Entries surfaced only through keyword matches, so the directory is not exhausted.
(3) No EDEBO register or NAQA result was returned for any institution. Existence, licence, NAQA accreditation and recognition therefore all remain gaps for every candidate. A Study in Ukraine directory listing is recorded only as a 'government' source showing that the institution is presented to foreigners; it is not evidence of a licence or accreditation.

NOT FOUND (search returned nothing, which is not evidence of anything): Petro Mohyla Black Sea National University (Mykolaiv) medical institute; International European University; Odesa International Medical University; Lviv Medical University; Kyiv International University. These remain unconfirmed leads for a future search.

CONTEXT LEADS:
- Visit Ukraine (Oct 2024) and NTU KhPI news (1 Nov 2024) cite MES statistics of 27,000+ foreign students in total, with medicine as the leading specialty at about 4,400 (https://www.kpi.kharkov.ua/eng/2024/11/29/ntu-khpi-is-among-the-top-3-university-leaders-in-ukraine-by-the-number-of-foreign-students/ ; https://visitukraine.today/blog/5241/how-many-foreign-students-are-there-in-ukraine-and-what-they-study-data-from-the-ministry-of-education-and-science).
- The Study in Ukraine portal (studyinukraine.gov.ua) states a range of EUR 1,500-5,000 per year for medical programmes, and says distance/online learning is not available for MBBS programmes. Another page on the same portal conflicts on flexibility. The portal metadata looked stale (https://studyinukraine.gov.ua/fees-and-scholarships/ ; https://studyinukraine.gov.ua/program_cat/study-mbbs-in-ukraine/).
- Careers360 reports that in 2022 only 1,438 of 5,333 Indian graduates with Ukrainian MBBS cleared India's licensing screening test (FMGE), about 27%. This is a third-party statement about the licensing test, not about recognition.

EXCLUDED INSTITUTIONS: Results for Bogomolets, Ternopil, Lviv, Zaporizhzhia, Bukovinian, Odesa, Poltava and Kharkiv NMU were ignored. The Bogomolets 2014 notices (nmuofficial.com) are cited only as context for Donetsk and Luhansk.

All 10 searches were standard mode; extended mode was not used and no pages were fetched. Everything here is a lead from search results, mostly in the search tool's own summary wording, so treat it as paraphrase unless marked 'as returned'. Excluded institutions that came up in results were left out: KhNMU, ONMU, IFNMU, Dnipro SMU and ZSMPhU.

Gaps (no result found, which is not evidence either way):
(a) Zaporizhzhia National University: both queries for it returned only ZSMPhU (excluded), so its medical faculty and any foreign-student programmes are unverified.
(b) Oles Honchar Dnipro National University: no result on any medical programme.
(c) King Danylo University (private, Ivano-Frankivsk): THE lists law, IT, architecture, construction, design, management and humanities, with no medicine or dentistry. Not added as a candidate.
(d) International University of Economics and Humanities named after Stepan Demianchuk (Rivne): no results.
(e) Odesa International Medical University, Kharkiv International Medical University and Lviv Medical Institute/University (private): no results for any of them.
(f) No results came back for Zhytomyr, Chernihiv, Kropyvnytskyi or Poltava (non-excluded) medical programmes. Those cities still need searches.

Other leads:
- MAUP (Interregional Academy of Personnel Management, private, Kyiv): Kyiv Post says it teaches about 2,000 foreigners across six departments, but it is not described as medical. Not added.
- Study in Ukraine portal pages (studyinukraine.gov.ua/?p=6548, ?p=7530, ?p=8369, ?p=228) rank institutions by foreign students and invitations. They are worth capturing by hand to list more medical and pharmacy providers.

I used 10 standard WebSearch calls, no extended mode and no WebFetch. The search tool returns a summary, not raw snippets. Text in double quotes inside 'says' is wording the tool presented as quoted from the result. Everything else is the tool's paraphrase. None of it has been verified.

ACCESS LIMITATIONS AND GAPS:
(1) No search covered Kyiv International University (KIU) because of the search budget. It is still an open lead.
(2) The search for a private 'Lviv Medical University' or 'Lviv Medical Institute' returned only Danylo Halytsky LNMU, which is excluded. Not finding the private institution is not evidence that it does not exist. It is still an open lead.
(3) The EDEBO register, the Ministry of Education licence register and the NAQA registry could not be checked. No candidate's current licence status is confirmed.
(4) Government portal URLs (universities.studyinukraine.gov.ua, studyinukraine.gov.ua) came up as results, but the tool showed little of their content. They could be opened in a later capture step.

ATTRIBUTION ERROR BY THE SEARCH TOOL: the tool's summary said the kmu.edu.ua page about the 'Dnipro Institute of Medicine and Public Health' (dimh.kmu.edu.ua) belonged to King Danylo University. Other results show kmu.edu.ua is Kyiv Medical University's domain. King Danylo University uses ukd.edu.ua, and its results show no medical faculty. I did not adopt the tool's attribution.

DOMAIN AMBIGUITY: dmu.edu.ua results were linked by the tool to Dnipro State Medical University, which is excluded. They are not evidence for the private Dnipro Medical Institute.

OTHER INSTITUTIONS THAT CAME UP BUT ARE NOT RECORDED AS CANDIDATES:
- Taras Shevchenko National University of Kyiv: appeared only as aggregator pages with no medical content in the summary. It may be worth a separate search.
- Ivano-Frankivsk NMU and Danylo Halytsky LNMU: in the exclusion list.

Kharkiv Medical Academy of Post-graduate Education is recorded only as a postgraduate-only lead from a Wikipedia result title.

criticNotes: Six WebSearch calls were made in standard mode. Four returned results. The last two were refused because the shared per-turn web search budget (200) was used up. That is a limit on access, not evidence that nothing is missing. The two searches that never ran were meant to check (a) the Dnipro Medical Institute of Traditional and Non-Traditional Medicine, and (b) Zaporizhzhia National University's medical faculty and Kyiv International University (dentistry). These names, and others such as the Zhytomyr Medical Institute, Kyiv National University of Technologies and Design (pharmacy) and the Kharkiv Medical Academy of Postgraduate Education (likely postgraduate only), come from prior knowledge, not search results. They are not returned as candidates. They should be checked in a later run before anything is concluded. Two notes on the results that did come back. First, the Kharkiv International Medical University search mostly returned material on Kharkiv National Medical University, which is already in the register. Second, studyinukraine.gov.ua/?p=7530 and ?p=6548 appeared in the results, but the tool returned no content from them that could be tied to a candidate. All candidate facts are search-result leads. None have been checked on .ua or .gov.ua pages, which this environment cannot open.

admissionLeads.text: 2026 sessions (search-tool summary of a kmu.edu.ua Admission Requirements page; the exact one of several URLs was not attributed): two admission sessions in 2026, the first 23–30 April and the second 6 July to 1 November.

An older, undated KMU page says international students are admitted twice a year: Fall Semester 1 July – 15 December, Spring Semester 15 January – 15 April. A 2025 page lists a summer session 7 July – 1 November.

Invitation-letter documents (consistent across KMU admission pages): scanned passport first page, school certificate with academic records, signed personal data consent form, and an application addressed to the Rector. Indian nationals also need a NEET qualification certificate. The university "decides whether or not to issue an Invitation Letter" after reviewing the documents.

Documents usually need legalization in the home country. On arrival applicants register in person at the International Faculty and "are informed of the date for two writing tests": language (English or Ukrainian) and Chemistry. The 2026 page adds that Biology may be tested.

Admission routes: in person in Kyiv, in person in Poland, or remotely. The Kyiv route is an electronic invitation letter, then a visa application, then a faculty application. The 2026 page describes an electronic invitation letter via the Study in Ukraine portal, only for people living in the EU or with visa-free access, for the Polish campus.
Ukrainian national rules: the discovery notes that admission follows national rules. No specific KMU statement on minimum grades or English-proficiency certificates was returned.
